overall: AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged: it could not determine whether a member listed as present was present, so it did not find the revised minutes inaccurate. AG noted concerns about adjournment vote recording and roll-call voting, with a reminder, but ordered no remedy.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the Feb. 18, 2021 minutes still list a member as present, though she says she was absent, after revision under OML 2022-52.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we are constrained to find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it approved revised minutes of the February 18, 2021, meeting.

allegations.summary: AG noted concern that the adjournment vote was recorded as 'Motion carried unanimously' though only three of five listed members actually voted. No violation was found.
allegations.key_passage: However, only three of the five members who were listed as present for the meeting actually voted to adjourn the meeting.

allegations.summary: AG observed the final adjournment vote was not taken by roll call despite remote participation, and reminded the Board of its obligations. No violation finding was made.
allegations.key_passage: The failure to vote by roll call further impeded our and the public’s ability to determine whether Ms. Pelletier was present during the February 18, 2021, meeting and underscores the importance of the requirement that votes be taken by roll call when members participate remotely.
